claim: HIPAA's definitions, at 45 CFR 160.103, make a covered entity one of three things: "(1) A health plan. (2) A health care clearinghouse. (3) A health care provider who transmits any health information in electronic form in connection with a transaction covered by this subchapter."
quote: Covered entity means: ( 1 ) A health plan. ( 2 ) A health care clearinghouse. ( 3 ) A health care provider who transmits any health information in electronic form in connection with a transaction covered by this subchapter.

claim: Those transactions are financial and administrative, such as health care claims, eligibility for and enrollment in a health plan, premium payments, and referral certification and authorization.
quote: Transaction means the transmission of information between two parties to carry out financial or administrative activities related to health care.

claim: ...health care claims...
quote: Health care claims or equivalent encounter information.

claim: ...eligibility for and enrollment in a health plan...
quote: Enrollment and disenrollment in a health plan.

claim: ...eligibility for a health plan...
quote: Eligibility for a health plan.

claim: ...premium payments...
quote: Health plan premium payments.

claim: ...and referral certification and authorization.
quote: Referral certification and authorization.

claim: CMS is part of HHS.
quote: CMS stands for Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services within the Department of Health and Human Services.

claim: CMS sums up the provider test in one line: "Providers who submit HIPAA transactions, like claims, electronically are covered."
quote: Providers who submit HIPAA transactions , like claims, electronically are covered.

claim: Its list of health plans includes employer-sponsored health plans.
quote: Employer-sponsored health plans

claim: Section 160.103 makes a business associate a person who, on behalf of a covered entity, "creates, receives, maintains, or transmits protected health information" for a regulated function.
quote: On behalf of such covered entity or of an organized health care arrangement (as defined in this section) in which the covered entity participates, but other than in the capacity of a member of the workforce of such covered entity or arrangement, creates, receives, maintains, or transmits protected health information for a function or activity regulated by this subchapter

claim: ...and names "A person that offers a personal health record to one or more individuals on behalf of a covered entity"...
quote: A person that offers a personal health record to one or more individuals on behalf of a covered entity.

claim: ...and subcontractors of business associates.
quote: A subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains, or transmits protected health information on behalf of the business associate.

claim: A health plan, per the FTC's tool, likely is a covered entity.
quote: 3a. Are you a health plan? Yes HIPAA: As HHS guidance about entities covered by HIPAA explains, you likely are a HIPAA covered entity subject to the HIPAA Rules.

claim: A health care provider such as a doctor, dentist, psychologist, hospital, health care clinic or pharmacy likely is a covered entity.
quote: 3b. Are you a health care provider, such as a doctor, dentist, psychologist, hospital, health care clinic, or pharmacy?

claim: ...you likely are a covered entity.
quote: As HHS guidance about entities covered by HIPAA explains, you likely are a covered entity subject to the HIPAA Rules .

claim: Consumers need a prescription to access your app: you may be a covered health care provider.
quote: 5. Do consumers need a prescription to access your app? Yes HIPAA: You may be a HIPAA covered health care provider and therefore subject to the HIPAA Rules .

claim: You develop, offer or operate the app on behalf of a covered entity, such as a hospital, doctor's office, health insurer or a health plan's wellness program, or you are a subcontractor to one...
quote: Are you developing, offering, or operating an app on behalf of a HIPAA covered entity (such as a hospital, doctor’s office, health insurer, or health plan’s wellness program)? Or are you acting as a subcontractor to another entity providing services to a covered entity?

claim: ...you likely are a business associate.
quote: You likely are a HIPAA business associate , and therefore subject to the HIPAA Security Rule and specific provisions of the HIPAA Privacy and Breach Notification Rules

claim: None of these: you likely are not covered by HIPAA, though other laws, like the FTC Act, may apply.
quote: You likely are not covered by HIPAA. (Other laws, like the FTC Act, may also apply, but we’ll get to that.)

claim: The same tool says the HIPAA Rules "likely wouldn't apply to consumer health information maintained in an app that isn't offered by a HIPAA covered entity or its business associate, even if the health information originated from a covered entity or business associate."
quote: the HIPAA Rules likely wouldn’t apply to consumer health information maintained in an app that isn’t offered by a HIPAA covered entity or its business associate, even if the health information originated from a covered entity or business associate.

claim: HHS's Office for Civil Rights publishes its own health-app scenarios, which the FTC's tool points to.
quote: For additional guidance on whether HIPAA applies to your mobile app, visit OCR’s Resources for Mobile Health Apps Developers , which includes hypothetical health app use scenarios and links to frequently asked questions (FAQs).

claim: The rule's text says a breach of security includes an unauthorized acquisition "that occurs as a result of a data breach or an unauthorized disclosure".
quote: A breach of security includes an unauthorized acquisition of unsecured PHR identifiable health information in a personal health record that occurs as a result of a data breach or an unauthorized disclosure.

claim: The FTC's own example is sharing users' health information with an ad network without consent.
quote: suppose you share your users’ medical information along with their mobile identifiers with an ad network for the purpose of targeted marketing without first getting the person’s consent.

claim: The FTC's guidance tells companies not to make false or misleading claims that they are "HIPAA Compliant," "HIPAA Secure," "HIPAA Certified" or the like.
quote: don’t make false or misleading claims that you are “HIPAA Compliant,” “HIPAA Secure,” “HIPAA Certified” or the like.

claim: FAQ: covered entities are health plans, health care clearinghouses and health care providers that transmit health information electronically in standard transactions such as claims.
quote: The HIPAA Rules apply to you if you are a HIPAA covered entity – a health plan, a health care provider that conducts standard health care transactions electronically, or a health care clearinghouse.
